Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract, then use the required fish-control bookshelf and the visual-evidence skill before proposing or editing the controller. I’ll keep the implementation to exactly one candidate and verify both required documentation updates.

The workspace is the common-naive-seed case, so the bookshelf consultation is mandatory now. Its visual skill also requires comparing the best finite rollout with an informative failure and cross-checking images against metrics/diagnostics; I’m gathering those before selecting the transferable mechanism.

The evidence narrows the problem: all sampled candidates self-propel on the same compact-wake route, while terminal mechanisms mostly change crossing geometry. The score-best posterior residual arrives fastest but adds tail dwell/load and remains tangential; force-deficit and line-rate variants also remain in the wide-crossing class. I’m consulting the bookshelf now for a genuinely different bounded mechanism, not another gain or threshold tweak.

The bookshelf’s useful invariant is CPG-style control allocation: preserve the autonomous traveling carrier, and modulate where a bounded directional residual enters based on observed joint state. I’ll test one mechanism only—redistribute the score-best posterior miss residual toward the anterior rhythmic channel when the tail loses angle/rate reserve—so the candidate stays close to the fastest sampled capture while directly addressing its tail dwell and load penalty.

The candidate file now contains the single reserve-aware allocator. The inherited evidence also supports a durable negative lesson: neither force-deficit feedback nor predicted-capture release escaped the wide terminal class, while the posterior residual’s faster capture came with a specific tail-state cost. I’m folding that distinction into reusable guidance rather than recording an iteration diary.

The first mandated check exposed a workspace-metadata defect before evaluating my changes: `README.md` marks the same guidance parent twice, while the checker requires exactly one copied-parent marker. I’m inspecting the checker to repair only that duplicated marker, then I’ll rerun the prescribed checks.

All three prescribed runner checks now pass. I’m doing one additional algebraic audit focused on the new mechanism: a joint/geometry grid will verify finite bounded commands, exact left-right reflection, and nonzero behavioral difference from the sampled posterior-only residual. No CFD will be run here.

The extra audit hit a Julia soft-scope issue in the test harness itself before testing the policy. I’m rerunning the same audit inside a function so the result is meaningful; the prescribed checks remain passed.

The candidate-specific and reusable guidance artifacts are complete, and local algebraic checks pass. I’m now invoking the requested check-runner as an independent final audit of the three prescribed checks; it should only report PASS/FAIL and must not run CFD or edit the policy.

Implemented exactly one candidate: a joint-reserve-aware redirect allocator that transfers terminal residual authority from the tail to the anterior joint as tail angle/rate reserve decreases.

Updated:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1)
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1), including the required bookshelf transfer block
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:110), documenting force/corridor negatives and the posterior-residual boundary

All independent check-runner checks passed: guidance materiality, Julia policy contract, parameter schema, and solver boundary. A 13,230-state audit found finite bounded commands, zero reflection error, and an active allocator mechanism. No CFD was run. I also removed one duplicated parent marker from `README.md` that initially prevented the mandated checker from resolving the assigned parent.
